title: Namespaces
learning_outcomes: Explain what namespaces contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: declaring namespaces.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Advanced object design is about collaboration and stable contracts. Interfaces, composition, dependency injection, namespaces, and autoloading help change or test parts independently. In this lesson, focus on declaring namespaces; then compare it with fully qualified names. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use namespaces when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Namespaces
content_blocks.code:
<?php
interface Notifier { public function send(string $message): string; }
final class LogNotifier implements Notifier { public function send(string $message): string { return "logged: " . $message; } }
echo (new LogNotifier())->send("ready") . PHP_EOL;

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
